2027-02-16.title: Tuesday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Sarah shall be her name; Isaac is promised
By grace you have been saved through faith
You will know them by their fruits
2027-02-16.verse: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
theo: God now turns to Sarai: “you shall not call her Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name. I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her.” And the father of believers falls on his face and laughs: “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?” Then he makes a quieter, more human prayer: “O that Ishmael might live in your sight!” He already has a son; perhaps he would settle for that. God's answer is both firm and tender: “No, but your wife Sarah shall bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac.” Isaac means “he laughs”: God will turn Abraham's doubtful laugh into the laughter of joy. And Ishmael is not forgotten: “As for Ishmael, I have heard you; I will bless him.” God's plan is larger than our hopes, and kinder than our fears.

Paul tells the Ephesians that every Christian life begins the way Isaac's did: with something impossible that only God can do. “You were dead through the trespasses and sins in which you once lived… But God, who is rich in mercy, out of the great love with which he loved us even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ.” Our fasting does not buy this life: “by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” Yet grace is not idle: “we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works.” That is why Jesus gives a simple test: “You will know them by their fruits… every good tree bears good fruit.” St Augustine says that when God crowns our merits he is crowning his own gifts (in substance). In the Fast we do not try to grow fruit by our own strength; we stay grafted to the One who makes the tree good.
outline: Ask: have you ever laughed at something God promised because it seemed impossible?
Sarah's new name and Isaac's promise.
Dead in trespasses, made alive with Christ.
“By grace you have been saved through faith.”
live: Thank God for one undeserved gift (Ephesians 2:8)
Write down three gifts in your life you did nothing to earn, and thank God for each tonight.
Ask someone close to you which good fruit they see in your life, and which they would like to see.
2027-02-16.prayer: God rich in mercy, you gave Abraham a son when it was impossible and turned his laughter of doubt into the laughter of joy. You made us alive with Christ when we were dead in our sins. Let us never forget that all is your gift. Make us good trees, rooted in your grace, bearing the fruit of good works which you prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive grace upon grace, the gift we could never earn: Christ himself, who makes us alive.

quick: God renamed Sarai as Sarah and promised Abraham a son, Isaac.
We are saved by grace through faith, for the good works God prepared.
Jesus says: you will know them by their fruits.
2027-02-16.action: Thank God tonight for three gifts you did not earn.
2027-02-16.question: What fruit does my life bear when no one is watching?

family.explain: Grace means a gift we did not earn. Our life, our family, our baptism: all are gifts from God. God gives us his love first, and then helps us do good works, like a tree that grows fruit.
family.intention: We pray that our family may bear good fruit: kindness, patience and joy.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit do we see in each other?”

illus: A retired headmaster in Punalur planted a jackfruit tree when his first grandchild was born. For years it gave only leaves, and his neighbours told him to cut it down. He watered it, manured it and waited. In the eighth year it gave so much fruit that he sent jackfruit to every house on the lane. When people thanked him he would point at the tree and say: do not thank me. I only waited. It did what it was made to do.

pm.open: God rich in mercy, we are alive only by your grace. Make us bear fruit for you. Amen.
share: Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? (Genesis 17:17). What promise of God seems too good to be true for me?
By grace you have been saved through faith (Ephesians 2:8). Do I still try to earn God's love?
You will know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:16). What fruit would others say my life bears?
pm.resp: Lord, by your grace make us fruitful.
interc: For couples who long for a child.
For those who feel spiritually dead and far from God.
For preachers and teachers, that they may be true prophets known by good fruit.
For children and young people growing in faith.
For those whose prayers seem unanswered.
pm.close: Father, you are rich in mercy and you made us alive with your Son. Keep us rooted in your grace, so that our lives may bear the good fruit you prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God promised Abraham a son by Sarah, and Abraham fell on his face and laughed: can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? (Genesis 17:17). God did not take back the promise. He named the child Isaac, he laughs.

Abraham also prayed: O that Ishmael might live in your sight! And God answered: as for Ishmael, I have heard you; I will bless him (Genesis 17:18, 20). God's plan is larger than our hopes and kinder than our fears.

Paul says that we too were given life when it was impossible: you were dead through the trespasses and sins... but God, who is rich in mercy, made us alive together with Christ. By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God (Ephesians 2:1, 4–5, 8).

Grace bears fruit. Jesus says: you will know them by their fruits; every good tree bears good fruit (Matthew 7:16–17). Our fasting does not earn God's love; it opens us to receive it, so that we may bear the fruit he has prepared. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham was a hundred years old and Sarah was ninety when God promised them a baby. Abraham laughed! But God kept his promise, and baby Isaac was born. Nothing is impossible for God. God's love is a gift; we cannot buy it, only say thank you.

intro: Theme: “By grace you have been saved through faith.”
God's impossible gift to Abraham, God's impossible gift to us, and the fruit that grace bears.

sub: “O that Ishmael might live in your sight!”
Isaac: God turns doubt into joy.
q: The nations shall see your vindication, and all the kings your glory; and you shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the Lord will give.
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Bring to God the promise you find hardest to believe, and pray over it each day this week.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
For we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand to be our way of life.
points.apply: Make a good confession this week, receiving mercy as pure gift.

q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit to practise deliberately for the rest of the Fast.

concl: What is impossible for us is the beginning of God's work.
Grace received in faith becomes fruit in good works.
2027-02-16.resolve: Thank God each night of the Fast for one gift you did not earn.
